items.jp: 肉か さかなを 食べたいです
items.kana: にくかきごうさかなをきごうたべたいです

structure_explanation.en: Here the か appears between two nouns, 肉 and さかな, with the meaning 'A or B' (same family as the target か～か, in the simple form 'A か B'). The を afterward marks this set 'meat or fish' as the object. The verb is in the desiderative form 食べたい (want to eat), made polite with です.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Aqui o か aparece entre dois substantivos, 肉 e さかな, com o sentido de 'A ou B' (mesma família do alvo か～か, na forma simples 'A か B'). O を depois marca esse conjunto 'carne ou peixe' como objeto. O verbo está na forma desiderativa 食べたい (querer comer), educada com です.

translation_literal.en: I want to eat either meat or fish.

translation.en: I want to eat meat or fish.

conjugation_note.en: stem 食べ of 食べる before the auxiliary たい
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz 食べ de 食べる antes do auxiliar たい

conjugation_note.en: たい (desiderative) on the verb stem
conjugation_note.pt-BR: たい (desiderativo) sobre a raiz do verbo

conjugation_note.en: です gives a polite tone to the たい form
conjugation_note.pt-BR: です dá tom educado à forma たい

findings.issue: Literal pt leaves か untranslated as a raw '(か)' and ends in near-gibberish ('comer-querer é'); it never conveys か = 'ou', unlike lit_en ('either meat or fish') and unlike the literal style used everywhere else in the batch.

items.kana: かれわげんきなようです

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the pattern 〜様です (yōdesu), which indicates that something 'seems/appears to be' based on what is observed. Since 元気 is a na-adjective (adjectival noun), it links to 様 with the particle な: 元気な様です. The topic 彼 (he) is marked by は, and です closes the sentence in the polite register.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa o padrão 〜様です (você), que indica que algo 'parece/aparenta ser' com base no que se observa. Como 元気 é um adjetivo-な (substantivo adjetival), ele se liga a 様 com a partícula な: 元気な様です. O tópico 彼 (ele) é marcado por は, e です fecha a frase no registro polido.

translation_literal.en: As for him, he looks like he is well (healthy/energetic).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a ele, está com aparência de estar bem (saudável/com energia).

translation.en: He seems to be doing well.

gloss.en: in good health, full of energy
gloss.pt-BR: bem de saúde, cheio de energia

conjugation_note.en: な-adjective (元気); appears with な before 様
conjugation_note.pt-BR: adjetivo-な (元気); aparece com な antes de 様

gloss.en: (links the な-adjective to the noun 様)
gloss.pt-BR: (liga o adjetivo-な ao substantivo 様)

role.en: linking auxiliary (連体形 form of だ)
role.pt-BR: auxiliar de ligação (forma 連体形 de だ)

conjugation_note.en: な (attributive) form of だ, used because 元気 is a な-adjective
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma な (atributiva) de だ, usada porque 元気 é adjetivo-な

gloss.en: appearance of, look of (it seems that)

role.en: head of the 様です pattern (expresses appearance/conjecture)
role.pt-BR: núcleo do padrão 様です (expressa aparência/conjectura)

findings.issue: The conjectural auxiliary よう is written with the kanji 様; standard modern/textbook orthography for 〜ようです (the N3 target pattern) is kana, and 様 invites the misreading さま. Tokens[4].s should change accordingly (kana/romaji already read よう).

Machine-translation artifact: the romanization 'yōdesu' in expl_en became '(você)' in the pt explanation — '〜様です (você)' is nonsense and will confuse learners into linking the pattern to the pronoun 'você'.
findings.current: A frase usa o padrão 〜様です (você), que indica
findings.proposed: A frase usa o padrão 〜様です (yō desu), que indica

items.jp: 日曜日は本を読んだり音楽を聞いたりします
items.kana: にちようびわほんをよんだりおんがくをきいたりします

structure_explanation.en: The target is the structure 〜たり〜たりする, which lists representative activities (not exhaustively): the idea is 'I do things like X and Y, among others'. Each verb goes into the た form and gains り: 読む becomes 読んだり (with 〜だり because of the voiced sound) and 聞く becomes 聞いたり. At the end, します (polite form of する) ties the list of actions together. 日曜日は marks 'Sunday' as the topic/setting of the sentence.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O alvo é a estrutura 〜たり〜たりする, que lista atividades representativas (não exaustivas): a ideia é 'faço coisas como X e Y, entre outras'. Cada verbo vai na forma た e ganha り: 読む vira 読んだり (com 〜だり por causa do som sonoro) e 聞く vira 聞いたり. No fim, します (forma polida de する) amarra a lista de ações. 日曜日は marca 'domingo' como o tópico/cenário da frase.

translation_literal.en: On Sunday, I do things like reading books and listening to music.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao domingo, faço coisas como ler livro e ouvir música.

translation.en: On Sundays I do things like read books and listen to music.
translation.pt-BR: Aos domingos eu faço coisas como ler livros e ouvir música.

role.en: verb of the list of actions

conjugation_note.en: 〜た form of 読む (the base 読ん combines with 〜だり)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma 〜た de 読む (a base 読ん combina com 〜だり)

role.en: verb of the list of actions

conjugation_note.en: 〜た form of 聞く (聞い + たり)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma 〜た de 聞く (聞い + たり)

role.en: main verb (closes the たり〜たり structure)
role.pt-BR: verbo principal (fecha a estrutura たり〜たり)

conjugation_note.en: 連用形 (連体ます-stem) of する
conjugation_note.pt-BR: base conetiva 〜ます de する

conjugation_note.en: ます in the polite affirmative present
conjugation_note.pt-BR: ます no presente afirmativo polido

findings.issue: EN note on し (of します) names the wrong conjugation category: '連体ます-stem' should be 連用形 (masu-stem); 連体形 is the attributive form. PT note uses pt-PT spelling 'conetiva' instead of BR 'conectiva'.
findings.current: 連用形 (連体ます-stem) of する / base conetiva 〜ます de する
findings.proposed: 連用形 (masu-stem) of する / base conectiva (〜ます) de する

items.jp: 彼は注意が足りないと息子をしかった。
items.kana: かれわちゅういがたりないとむすこをしかった。

structure_explanation.en: Same construction: 君が怒る ('you getting angry') nominalized by の, predicate もっともだ ('it's natural'). The difference is も instead of は: も means 'also', suggesting that, besides something already said, it's also understandable that you get angry. が marks 君 as the internal subject.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: 彼は estabelece 'ele' como tópico. O trecho 注意が足りない ('falta atenção / não há cuidado bastante') é uma oração interna fechada pela partícula と, que aqui cita o conteúdo/motivo da repreensão ('dizendo que...'). 注意が足りない usa 足りる ('ser suficiente') na forma negativa 足りない. A frase termina em 息子をしかった ('repreendeu o filho'), com を marcando o objeto direto e た marcando o passado.

translation_literal.en: He, [saying] that attention isn't enough, scolded his son.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Ele, [dizendo] que a atenção não é suficiente, repreendeu o filho.

translation.pt-BR: Ele repreendeu o filho dizendo que ele não tinha cuidado suficiente.

conjugation_note.en: stem of 足りる ('to suffice') in the 連用形 form, to which the negation ない attaches
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz de 足りる ('bastar') na forma 連用形, à qual se liga a negação ない

conjugation_note.en: negative auxiliary ない; 足りない = 'to be insufficient / to be lacking'
conjugation_note.pt-BR: auxiliar negativo ない; forma 足りない = 'não ser suficiente / faltar'

conjugation_note.en: 連用形 (音便) stem of しかる ('to scold'), to which the past た attaches
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz 連用形 (音便) de しかる ('repreender'), à qual se liga た de passado

findings.issue: expl_en explains a completely different sentence (君が怒るのももっともだ: の-nominalization, もっともだ, も vs は) — copy-paste error. It matches nothing in this sentence and contradicts expl_pt, which correctly explains the quotative と + しかった structure.
findings.current: Same construction: 君が怒る ('you getting angry') nominalized by の, predicate もっともだ ('it's natural'). The difference is も instead of は...
findings.proposed: 彼は establishes 'he' as the topic. The stretch 注意が足りない ('attention is lacking / he wasn't careful enough') is an inner clause closed by the particle と, which here quotes the content/reason of the scolding ('saying that...'). 注意が足りない uses 足りる ('to be enough') in its negative form 足りない. The sentence ends in 息子をしかった ('scolded his son'), with を marking the direct object and た marking the past.

items.jp: そういうところが好きなの。
items.kana: そういうところがすきなの。

structure_explanation.en: The structure is [そういうところ]=topic marked by が + [好き]=na-adjective meaning 'to like'. 好き uses が to mark THE thing one likes. At the end, なの (なだ + the particle の) gives an explanatory and gentle tone, common in feminine or affectionate speech.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura é [そういうところ]=tópico marcado por が + [好き]=adjetivo-nominal (na) que significa 'gostar'. O 好き usa が para marcar AQUILO de que se gosta. No fim, なの (なだ + a partícula の) dá um tom explicativo e suave, comum na fala feminina ou afetuosa.

translation_literal.en: This kind of place is what I like, you know.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Esse tipo de ponto (lugar) é o que eu gosto, sabe.

translation.pt-BR: É justamente isso que eu gosto em você.

role.en: verb that forms the fixed expression そういう ('of that kind')
role.pt-BR: verbo que forma a expressão fixa そういう ('desse tipo')

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of いう, here within the phrase そういう
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de いう, aqui dentro da locução そういう

role.pt-BR: substantivo núcleo (aquilo de que se gosta)

role.en: copula auxiliary (form だ before の)
role.pt-BR: auxiliar de cópula (forma だ antes de の)

conjugation_note.en: な is the form of だ used before the explanatory particle の
conjugation_note.pt-BR: な é a forma de だ usada antes da partícula explicativa の

findings.issue: が is described as marking the topic. が marks the subject (the thing liked, with 好き); topics are marked by は. The very next sentence correctly says が marks the thing one likes, so the label 'topic' is a false particle-function claim.
findings.current: [そういうところ]=topic marked by が
findings.proposed: [そういうところ]=subject marked by が

findings.issue: Garbled decomposition: 'なだ' is not a word. なの = な (the form of だ used before の) + の, exactly as the な token note states. As written it teaches a false composition.
findings.current: なの (なだ + the particle の)
findings.proposed: なの (な, the form of だ used before の, + the particle の)

findings.issue: が é descrito como marcador de tópico. が marca o sujeito (aquilo de que se gosta, com 好き); tópico é marcado por は. Ensina uma função de partícula falsa, contradizendo a frase seguinte da própria explicação.
findings.current: [そういうところ]=tópico marcado por が
findings.proposed: [そういうところ]=sujeito marcado por が

findings.issue: Decomposição truncada: 'なだ' não existe. なの = な (forma de だ usada antes de の) + の, como diz a própria nota do token な.
findings.current: なの (なだ + a partícula の)
findings.proposed: なの (な, forma de だ usada antes de の, + a partícula の)

items.jp: 彼はどんなに苦しんだことだろう。
items.kana: かれわどんなにくるしんだことだろう。

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the pattern どんなに〜ことだろう, an exclamatory variant of どんなに〜ことか. どんなに means 'how much / how' and intensifies the verb 苦しんだ (suffered). The ending ことだろう turns it all into an exclamation charged with emotion, of the type 'how he must have suffered!', rather than a literal question. は marks 彼 (he) as the topic.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa o padrão どんなに～ことだろう, uma variante exclamativa de どんなに～ことか. どんなに significa 'o quanto / quão' e intensifica o verbo 苦しんだ (sofreu). O fecho ことだろう transforma tudo numa exclamação carregada de emoção, do tipo 'como ele deve ter sofrido!', em vez de uma pergunta literal. は marca 彼 (ele) como o tópico.

translation_literal.en: I wonder how much he suffered.

conjugation_note.en: だ-connective form (音便) of 苦しむ; equivalent to 苦しんだ (past)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma だ-conectiva (音便) de 苦しむ; equivale a 苦しんだ (passado)

gloss.en: it must be / it will be

findings.issue: The past-tense auxiliary だ (た voiced after 苦しん) is left with null gloss/role, unlike every other past auxiliary in the file (cf. かかっ+た labelled 'auxiliar de passado'); the 苦しん note even points to it.
